sentence: This project studies how human pancreatic cells develop, to improve methods for making insulin-secreting cells from stem cells.
This project tries to find out how two proteins acting together worsen Alzheimer's disease, using laboratory models and human brain tissue.
This project studies how the mitochondria in sensory nerve cells control their sensitivity, and tests mild compounds that uncouple mitochondria in pain models.
This project tests a light-based imaging method that uses antibodies to find very small pancreatic cancer deposits during surgery.
This project studies how to improve responses to cancer immunotherapies and treat resistance to them in melanoma.
This project builds a framework using microfluidics and computing to test how existing drugs could reduce spleen congestion and anemia in sickle cell disease.
This project builds tools that control when Mycobacterium abscessus switches between its smooth and rough types, to see how the immune system responds to each.
This project studies how circular pieces of DNA outside chromosomes form, work and help cancers resist treatment.
This project builds a genetically engineered mouse model of Nut carcinoma to understand its early stages.
This project builds AI tools that use brain scans to find individual brain patterns and predict cognitive and psychiatric traits.
This project studies how rhabdomyosarcoma depends on histone demethylases and tests a drug that blocks them.
This project builds blood-based and imaging-based tests to spot hepatocellular carcinoma early in patients with cirrhosis.
This project tests imaging scans that measure cells around prostate tumors, in patients and in a mouse model, to understand how the cancer develops.
This project studies how a family of microtubule-associated proteins controls transport inside nerve cell axons and their branch development.
This project studies how thyroid hormone signaling affects muscle stem cells during skeletal muscle regeneration after injury.
This project builds an exercise program based on regulating feelings and tests whether it raises physical activity in inactive breast cancer survivors.
This project uses brain imaging to study whether low dopamine levels are linked to depression in people with HIV and whether treatment raises them.
This project studies how a mutant gene changes brain circuits in the cerebellum across life in an inherited disease, spinocerebellar ataxia type 1.
This project studies how harmful environmental exposures and inflammation damage blood-forming stem cells and speed up blood aging.
This project builds statistical tools and a simulation to design and analyze cell village experiments that pool human stem cell lines.
